data.name: Your Quest
data.detailed_description:
You awaken to the dawn of a new world.
It's streams are clean, the forests lush and the local wildlife is hungry.
You're cold and in need of shelter as you hear other voices on the wind. You are not alone.

Your quest: Establish civilization and secure their safety in this new world.



Your Quest is a casual 2D Strategy/RPG with progressive gameplay where you gather resources to construct a village, craft new weapons and armor, and try to survive the depths of a procedurally generated dungeon under the surface.

If you would like to support development, you can "name your own price" on itch.io:

Features
  • Turn-based Combat
  • Village Building
  • Craftable Armor and Weapons
  • Village Raids
  • Procedurally generated dungeon



Controls
Keyboard
W/A/S/D: Movement
Enter: Interact and Menu Selection
Esc: Main Menu and Cancel
Ctrl + W/A/S/D: Turn in that direction
Ctrl + A/D when managing jobs: Increases/Decreases jobs by 10
I: Inventory

Xbox 360 Controller
Left Stick/D-Pad: Movement
A: Interact and Menu Selection
Start: Main Menu
B: Cancel
Left Shoulder + Left Stick/D-Pad: Turn in that direction
Left Shoulder + Left/Right on the Left Stick/D-Pad when managing jobs:
Increases/Decreases jobs by 10
Y: Inventory

reviews.review:
Your Quest is an indie strategy RPG that combines several gameplay genres into a single experience focused on survival, growth, and exploration. Developed and published by Oblivionburn Productions, the game places players in a remote wilderness where they must transform a small settlement into a thriving community while simultaneously managing resources, crafting equipment, battling enemies, and exploring dangerous underground locations. Although its presentation is relatively modest, the game offers a surprising amount of depth and freedom for players who enjoy long-term progression and strategic decision-making.

The foundation of the experience revolves around establishing and maintaining a settlement. Players begin with very little and must gradually gather resources to expand their community. Every new building, worker assignment, and upgrade contributes to the settlement's development, creating a satisfying sense of progression. Watching a tiny outpost slowly evolve into a productive village is one of the game's most rewarding aspects. The gradual expansion provides clear goals and gives players a strong incentive to continue improving their infrastructure.

Resource gathering forms the backbone of nearly every system in the game. Wood, stone, food, and other materials are required to support growth and unlock new opportunities. Players must carefully balance short-term needs with long-term ambitions, deciding whether resources should be invested in expansion, equipment, or defensive preparations. These choices add a layer of strategy that keeps the gameplay engaging throughout the adventure. The economy is simple enough to remain accessible but complex enough to make resource management feel meaningful.

Crafting plays a central role in progression. Materials collected through exploration and gathering can be transformed into tools, weapons, armor, and other useful items. This creates a satisfying gameplay loop where every expedition contributes to future success. Stronger equipment allows players to survive increasingly dangerous encounters, while improved tools help gather resources more efficiently. The interconnected nature of these systems ensures that no activity feels isolated from the broader progression structure.

Combat introduces another dimension to the experience through turn-based encounters that emphasize planning over reflexes. Players must consider their available resources, equipment, and positioning when confronting hostile creatures and other threats. While the combat system may not be as deep as those found in dedicated tactical RPGs, it provides enough strategic depth to remain engaging and complements the management aspects of the game effectively. Battles serve as meaningful tests of preparation rather than simple interruptions between exploration segments.

Exploration is one of the game's most enjoyable features. Beyond the settlement lies a world filled with opportunities, dangers, and hidden rewards. The procedurally generated dungeon system ensures that players constantly encounter new layouts, enemies, and challenges. Every descent into the underground areas feels unpredictable, encouraging curiosity and experimentation. The randomized nature of these environments significantly increases replayability and helps keep the experience fresh even after many hours of play.

The dungeon mechanics also provide a strong sense of risk and reward. Valuable resources and useful equipment can often be found in dangerous locations, forcing players to decide how much they are willing to risk for greater rewards. This tension enhances the exploration process and creates memorable moments where careful planning can lead to significant gains. The constant possibility of discovering something valuable helps maintain excitement throughout each expedition.

Village defense adds another strategic layer to the gameplay. As the settlement grows, it becomes a target for hostile forces. Players must prepare defenses and ensure their community can survive unexpected attacks. These threats prevent the management systems from becoming overly passive and encourage players to think ahead. Balancing economic growth with security becomes a recurring challenge that adds depth to the overall experience.

Visually, Your Quest adopts a simple two-dimensional presentation that prioritizes clarity and functionality over graphical sophistication. The pixel-art style and straightforward interface may not immediately impress players accustomed to modern high-budget productions, but they effectively communicate the information necessary to manage the settlement and navigate the world. The simplicity of the visuals allows the gameplay systems to remain the primary focus, which ultimately works in the game's favor.

The pacing is deliberately gradual. Progress is earned through consistent effort rather than rapid rewards, making the game particularly appealing to players who enjoy building something over time. Every new structure, crafted item, and successful expedition contributes to a larger sense of accomplishment. This measured progression creates a rewarding experience for patient players who appreciate seeing the results of their planning and dedication.

Like many independent projects, the game has limitations. Certain mechanics can feel less refined than those found in larger strategy or role-playing titles, and the presentation occasionally reveals the constraints of a small development team. However, these shortcomings are outweighed by the ambition of the design. The game successfully combines village management, crafting, exploration, and tactical combat into a cohesive package that offers far more depth than its modest appearance might suggest.

Ultimately, Your Quest succeeds because it provides a rewarding blend of strategy and role-playing elements within a framework built around gradual growth and exploration. The combination of settlement development, resource management, crafting systems, turn-based combat, and procedurally generated adventures creates a gameplay loop that remains engaging over extended periods. While it may not possess the visual polish or production values of larger releases, it offers enough depth and flexibility to satisfy players looking for an indie experience focused on progression and strategic planning. For fans of management-oriented RPGs and exploration-driven adventures, Your Quest delivers a surprisingly enjoyable journey that rewards patience, creativity, and careful decision-making.

Rating: 5/10
